title: Places, Devotees & Teachings
about: Shirdi and Dwarkamai, devotees from Hemadpant to Tatya, and teachings like Shraddha and Saburi - the places, people, and values woven around Sai Baba's life. Remembering these names from the Satcharitra strengthens the faith of those who read them.

entries.meaning: The village in Maharashtra where Baba spent his entire life
The ruined mosque where Baba lived; said to be a name he gave it himself
The hall Baba was carried to in procession to sleep in every second night
The sacred ash Baba gave devotees as a blessing from his dhuni
The sacred fire Baba kept burning day and night in Dwarkamai
The garden Baba himself planted and watered
The temple deity at whose gate Mhalsapati first called Baba 'Ya Sai'
Where villagers first saw the young Baba meditating under a neem tree
The building a devotee named Buti built, which later became Baba's samadhi mandir
The Khandoba temple priest whose greeting 'Ya Sai' gave Baba his name
A Shirdi villager, Bayajabai's son, who spent nearly his whole life with Baba
Author of the Satcharitra (born Govind Raghunath Dabholkar); the name was Baba's own gift to him
One of Baba's closest devotees; Baba said their bond spanned seventy-two lifetimes
Tatya's mother, whom Baba called his sister for seven lifetimes
A Deputy Collector and Gita scholar, one of Baba's most prominent devotees
A Bombay solicitor who asked Baba to cure 'the lameness of my mind,' not his leg
A devotee who spread Baba's fame through kirtans, at Baba's own urging
A devotee Baba called his mother; she organized the Chavadi procession
The villager whose lost mare Baba found; Baba came to Shirdi with his wedding procession
One of only seven devotees present in the mosque at Baba's mahasamadhi
The first of the two qualities Baba asked of devotees above all - faith
The second quality Baba asked for - patience, perseverance
The bag Baba used to collect alms daily from five chosen households
The offering Baba asked some devotees for, then gave away the same day - teaching non-attachment
The guru-worship festival celebrated at Shirdi since 1909
15 October 1918, the day Baba left his body
The festival born in 1897 when Baba merged a Muslim Urs with this Hindu celebration - a mark of Hindu-Muslim unity
'God is the Master of all' - a phrase Baba often spoke
